title: Data centre leaks 5,000 gallons of fuel into waterway after suspected 'computer glitch'
text: The leak (not pictured) is under investigation (Picture: Google Maps) A waterway has been polluted with thousands of gallons of fuel after it leaked from a data centre in New Jersey. Roughly 5,000 gallons of fuel leaked from a storage tank at Equinix’s NY2 data center in Secaucus and flowed into Anderson Creek – a narrow tributary running through the New Jersey Meadowlands wetland in the northeast of the US state – on Friday evening. Secaucus mayor Michael Gonnelli said the spill had been caused by a ‘computer glitch’. However,Equinix – the ‘largest global data center and colocation provider for enterprise network and cloud computing’,according to its website – said an investigation into the cause of the leak was still underway. Containment barriers and vacuum trucks were sent out to suck a mixture of diesel and water out of the creek in a bid to stop the pollution from spreading. The New Jersey Department of Environmental Protection (DEP) said the fuel did not reach the Hackensack River,a 45-mile-long river stretching through New Jersey and neighbouring New York,ultimately flowing into Newark Bay.
